increment_paragraph: **SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES** (USER DECISION 2026-11-14, "Go with 1, 2A and typed refinements for 3"; gateway rule 50, rule 30 pointer, contract specification §C04.19.6 amended, G05d, Lean `QCore.MemberValueHelper` and `r50` in `QCore.BodyClauseStanding`; [report](../../reports/scheduler-destroy-member-states/README.md)). `mk_http_thread_destroy` (`qcore-provider-libevent`) states `parent |-> #stale`, `session |-> #kept` and `request |-> #kept` on its released formal beside its unlink and release; the inline `mk_thread_destroy` gets a helper declaration (the `cb_destroy` member invocation, `callee |-> #stale`, `caller`/`data |-> #kept`, released), which the loader now admits (member invocations beside member-path states on one released formal, no hand-off; consumers still refuse it at a call). Rule 50 composes, in rule 30's body reading and the declaration's own frame only, a direct call of a unit `static` helper with its declaration in force that receives a `#stale` path's value (directly or through its one copy) at the formal it releases, its invocations closed and empty over the run's member facts: where every path takes the object exactly once so and nothing else carries the value, body evidence `50` is recorded beside `30`; a store below the declaration's own unlink's link member inside a followed helper no longer ends the reading. Evidence only: no consumer reads the composition. Seven of the eight premises carry typed refinements (`quant proposition`, `resource_lifecycle_v1`, `resource_premise_decomposition`, `resource_premise_flow_v1`, 19 atoms); four texts are narrowed; every premise name stays, `scheduler_callback_footprint` included (no consumer folds the run set rule 50 reads). Locks synced, both declarations pinned at 046accf6 and 66910c10. Measured base `89fa31d21` against tip `7bbea41df` on the LERI card's preparations: no status move on any route (system 103/341/4, slice 59/340/1 with 4 Pending, corpus 1,081/3,617/6, each unchanged), the declared check matching on all three; the corpus's five scheduler rows gain the 19 atoms as hypothesis dependencies, and `mk_http_thread_destroy`'s three states are now covered by body evidence `30` and `50` in `mk_http_thread.c` (a declared assumption at base).
status_paragraph: SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES (gateway rule 50, base `89fa31d21`, measured tip `7bbea41df`): `mk_http_thread_destroy` states three member-path states and typed refinements of seven of its eight scheduler premises; `mk_thread_destroy` has a helper declaration that rule 50's body reading composes (evidence only). All eight premise names stay Open source truth on the rows resting on the declaration. No status move: system custody 103/341/4, slice 59/340/1 with 4 Pending, corpus 1,081/3,617/6, unchanged; `mk_http_thread_destroy` becomes partly validated in the corpus (its member-path states covered by body evidence `30` and `50`).

ledger.text: Amended by SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES (gateway rule 50): the declaration now states parent |-> #stale, session |-> #kept and request |-> #kept (rule 30, body-checked in mk_http_thread.c), and rule 50's body reading composes the inline mk_thread_destroy's own helper declaration at the copy th = mth->parent (the parent's object released, its callee deleted and left stale, cb_destroy invoking nothing over the run's closed empty set), recorded as body evidence 50; seven premises carry typed refinements (19 quant proposition atoms with lifecycle introductions, decompositions and one flow per premise; evidence-only), and the parent embedding, callback footprint, coroutine and borrowed chain texts are narrowed to what no symbolic clause states. Every premise name stays: no consumer of mk_http_thread_destroy reads rule 50's composition or folds the cb_destroy run set (RULE50-CONSUMER-COMPOSITION), so none is discharged.

ledger.title: Rule 50's composition of a helper at a stale member's value is evidence only; no consumer reads it
ledger.text: SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES composes, in rule 30's body reading, a declared unit helper handed a #stale path's value (mk_http_thread_destroy's mk_thread_destroy(th), th = mth->parent) and records body evidence 50, including that the helper's cb_destroy invocation reads a closed empty run set. A consumer of the destroyer applies only its own states, so scheduler_callback_footprint and the stale take of parent stay what they were for the consumers' rows. DISCHARGE: carry the composed facts (the helper's member invocations, with rule 12n's run fold of their sets, and its states at the taken object) into the destroyer's consumer-visible reading, with Lean parity and a measured statement of the rows resting on it; then drop the callback footprint premise where the fold keeps them.

ledger.title: A helper destroyer (member invocations beside member-path states) refuses at a direct call and as a candidate
ledger.text: The loader admits member invocations beside member-path states on one released formal (SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES, C04.19.6 amended) so that rule 50 can compose the declaration; a consumer reading it at a direct call refuses member-path-direct and as a callback candidate reads it missing, as for every non-plain member-path declaration. Only mk_thread_destroy is declared so, and its one call (inside mk_http_thread_destroy) sits in an Unknown row. DISCHARGE: compose the invocation (C04.19.3 over the run's set) and the states (C04.19.6 direct call) at a direct call in that order, with Lean parity, and measure.

ledger.title: Rule 50 never composes a helper whose member invocation set is closed and non-empty
ledger.text: Rule 50 qualifies a helper only when each member invocation it states reads a closed empty set over the run's member facts; a closed non-empty set (candidates that run) leaves the take a declared assumption, because the candidates' effects on the taken object are not composed. Not measured beyond Monkey's mk_thread.cb_destroy (empty). DISCHARGE: compose each candidate's declaration in force (C04.19.7) at the helper's invocation inside the reading, with Lean parity.

ledger.title: mk_thread_destroy's pin identity also covers the ucontext variant, where its states are vacuous
ledger.text: quirin-audit pin records both header definitions of mk_thread_destroy (mk_thread_libco.h and mk_thread_ucontext.h) in one identity at 046accf6 and 66910c10. Neither audited configuration compiles the ucontext header; there the invocation and release hold as declared, callee is an embedded ucontext_t (no linked object, so #stale decides nothing) and data does not exist (the #kept state names no path). Recorded by SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES in the declaration's comment. DISCHARGE: a pin identity per definition site selected by configuration (or a per-variant declaration), or a statement that no route compiles the ucontext variant.

ledger.title: The member-path-direct refusal names a hand-off when the declaration states a member invocation
ledger.text: A direct call of a member-path declaration that is not plain refuses member-path-direct with the text "it states what it leaves at member paths of a formal's object beside a hand-off, which only a callback invocation composes"; for a helper destroyer (SCHEDULER-DESTROY-MEMBER-STATES, member invocations beside its states) the text is wrong about the reason (measured: mk_http_thread_destroy's own row at mk_http_thread.c:269). Diagnostic text only; the refusal is right. DISCHARGE: name the non-plain clause in the refusal and re-measure the row's content.
